name: Liberal conservatism
summary: Liberal conservatism combines conservative respect for inherited institutions, order and gradual change with liberal commitments to the rule of law, private property, constitutional government and a lightly regulated market. It accepts a limited welfare state and moderate environmentalism, and is divided between socially conservative and socially liberal strands. It is the mainstream of European centre-right parties such as the CDU and the Nordic conservatives.
scope: Mainstream modern European centre-right liberal conservatism (CDU programmes, Nordic conservative parties, Cameron-era UK Conservatives) with its Burkean roots (Reflections on the Revolution in France) and the sceptical conservatism of Oakeshott and Hayek. Excludes aristocratic, reactionary and national-populist conservatism, and strict libertarianism. Social issues are split between strands, so many answers are 0 or low confidence.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Liberal conservatism rests on constitutional, parliamentary government, and Burke defended Parliament as the seat of lawmaking.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Moderate environmental and welfare concern is accepted by the centre-right, though animals are not a core theme (inferred).

animal-use-humane.rationale: Accepts established farming and research with welfare regulation, consistent with gradual reform and light regulation (inferred).

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Burkean conservatism and the CDU programme stress responsibility of the strong for the weak through subsidiarity and the social market.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Burke and the CDU value civic duty and participation in institutions rather than withdrawal (inferred).

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Mainstream liberal conservatives do not treat media as an instrument of social control; inferred from their defence of free media and markets.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: This is a critical-theory (Gramscian) claim that liberal conservatives would not endorse as a description of their own order (inferred).

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Favours open trade and the market as beneficial to all; dependency theory is contrary to that view (inferred).

native-born-offices.rationale: Committed to equality before the law and integration of citizens, so reserving offices by birth is not a mainstream position (inferred).

party-own-road.rationale: The statement concerns communist parties, on which the ideology has no stake.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Favours open markets, trade and investment as routes to development, as in the social market economy (inferred).

return-lost-territory.rationale: Mainstream European centre-right accepts postwar borders and European integration, so demanding territory back is rejected (inferred).

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Equal citizenship under a constitution leaves no room for political leadership by descent (inferred).

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Postwar CDU-type parties built their constitutions on rejecting dictatorship, though they usually frame this as democracy rather than anti-fascism (inferred).

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: The CDU programme and centre-right tradition condemn Nazi and communist dictatorship together as totalitarian.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Mainstream historical consensus, which this strand generally accepts, makes slavery the main cause (inferred).

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Burkean respect for inheritance pulls toward preservation, while the liberal strand accepts contextualising or removing some monuments, so it is split.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Socially conservative and socially liberal strands differ on this, so no single position is documented.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Equal protection under the law is accepted, so equal services are plausible, though the issue is rarely addressed (inferred).

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Liberal conservatism holds constitutional government and the rule of law to be broadly valid, though Burke stressed local circumstances (inferred).

military-guardian-role.rationale: Constitutional government requires civilian control of the armed forces, and a political role for the military is rejected.

paid-care-work.rationale: Mainstream centre-right favours family support and subsidiarity over recasting unpaid care as paid labour (inferred).

filial-duty.rationale: The CDU programme stresses family and subsidiarity, from which a duty of mutual support is inferred.

office-by-exam.rationale: Burkean conservatives favour office through inherited institutions, election and appointment, not examination; inferred.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: A lightly regulated market favours open ownership, though strategic exceptions are accepted; inferred.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Socially conservative and socially liberal strands of the family split on divorce.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Burke held that representatives owe voters their judgment and not obedience; inferred from the representative-government tradition.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Centre-right parties have backed funded private pillars within a mixed system, but keep a state pay-as-you-go base.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Burke and the tradition treat property as a bedrock of liberty and inheritance; communal land tenure is opposed.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Constitutional government and the rule of law are core liberal commitments of the family.

single-official-language.rationale: The CDU programme stresses German-language integration while accepting minority languages; adherents split.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Open markets in property are favoured, though some centre-right parties restrict it; inferred.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: The family stresses equal treatment under law, so outcome-based discrimination tests are disfavoured; inferred.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Light-regulation market support makes broad condemnation of consumption unlikely; inferred.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Centre-right parties stress law and alliance obligations, so arming rebels is disfavoured; inferred.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: The programme stresses alliances of consent and the rule of law; inferred.

corporate-influence.rationale: Adherents see lobbying and party donations as a normal part of a pluralist democracy, wanting only transparency; inferred.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Liberal conservatives favour open civil society and open markets, so heavy restriction of foreign funding is unlikely; inferred.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Centre-right parties such as the CDU back family-supporting policy, though they also accept managed immigration; inferred.

residents-only-property.rationale: Private property and free movement of capital and people are core, so residency limits on buying are disfavoured; inferred.

job-guarantee.rationale: A limited welfare state and market economy mean jobs come from the private market, not state guarantees.

democratic-peace.rationale: Liberal conservatives generally support democracy promotion and liberal internationalism; inferred.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Rule of law and respect for inherited institutions imply a presumption of obedience to law, with limited room for resistance.

non-intervention.rationale: The CDU programme backs multilateral action and responsibility to protect, so intervention is sometimes legitimate.

industrial-unions.rationale: Not a defining issue; adherents accept unions but are split on how they should be organised.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Rule of law and equal citizenship rule out collective conspiracy claims against minorities.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The CDU programme defends marriage and the family as pillars of society; abolishing legal marriage is a radical break.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Constitutional government and the rule of law fit freedom of information, with exceptions for security; inferred.

local-production.rationale: Market economy and free trade are accepted, so long supply chains are fine; inferred.

informal-organisation.rationale: Burkean thought values lasting institutions and parties over informal groups.

national-law-over-international.rationale: The CDU programme is strongly pro-European and committed to international law, so national courts are not placed above it; inferred.

religious-nation.rationale: Strands emphasise Christian heritage, but the CDU programme stresses integration and civic belonging rather than a religious definition of the nation.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Inferred from commitment to sovereign states in a rules-based order rather than ritual submission.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: The CDU programme stresses solidarity and fiscal balancing, so keeping all revenue is not mainstream (inferred).

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Defends private property, including productive property, as the base of a free economy.

defeat-communism.rationale: Historically anti-communist and committed to liberal democracy, though modern positions on engagement vary (inferred).

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: The social market economy and subsidiarity accept private and independent providers within publicly funded systems.

religion-illusion.rationale: Respects religion as part of inherited tradition and doubts it will fade (inferred from Burke).

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Inferred from support for market economies as sources of prosperity.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Favours reform of law and attitudes within the existing economic order (inferred).

socialized-care.rationale: Subsidiarity and the family as the first unit of society point to private care (inferred).

purge-loanwords.rationale: Respects living tradition and gradual change in language rather than purges (inferred).

treaties-binding.rationale: The rule of law and inherited obligations favour binding treaties (inferred).

cooperative-communities.rationale: Prefers established nations, markets and private property to communal reorganisation (inferred).

majority-settlement.rationale: Constitutional and liberal commitments counsel against steering settlement by ethnicity (inferred).

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Sees the social market economy as a capitalist order that works, not a third way (inferred).

historical-land-claim.rationale: Liberal conservatism favours universal rule of law over ancestral claims; inferred.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Liberal conservatism rests on liberal democracy and rule of law, so denying a documented genocide is rejected; inferred.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Liberal conservatism commits to the rule of law and individual liberty; mainstream CDU and Nordic conservatives have decriminalised.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Liberal conservatism commits to constitutional government and a free opposition.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Mainstream liberal conservatives accept freedom of religion and separate civil from religious authority.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Inferred: modern European centre-right rejects colonial exploitation, though some adherents defend past empire.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Not addressed; inferred that mainstream conservatives would not endorse such a doctrinal duty.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Liberal conservatism favours constitutional change by law and rejects forcible removal.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Burkean liberal conservatives prefer representative institutions over direct participation.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Sceptical of abstract theory; prefers individual rights and equal treatment under law.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Social issues split between socially conservative and socially liberal strands.

assisted-dying.rationale: Split between conservative and liberal strands.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Liberal conservatives see left and right as real but combine liberal and conservative elements; inferred.

alienated-labor.rationale: Inferred: liberal conservatism defends private property and market work, rejecting the Marxist claim.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Inferred: mainstream liberal conservatives hold that Muslim citizens are compatible with liberal democracy.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Constitutional government rests on popular consent, though CDU programmes speak of responsibility before God.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Split between secularist and religious-tolerant strands.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Not addressed by sources; adherents split.

social-market-economy.rationale: The CDU's Hannover programme commits to the social market economy, while the Wikipedia definition stresses classical-liberal minimal intervention and the scope includes Hayek, so support is moderate.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Mainstream centre-right parties support national defence and NATO.

rich-first.rationale: Inferred: favours open markets with social safety nets rather than staged privilege.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Inferred: the CDU and Nordic conservatives are Atlanticist and committed to NATO and the EU.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Liberal conservatives accept constitutional monarchy where it exists but support merit and election for offices of state, so hereditary succession of a leader is not endorsed.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Inferred: favours a lightly regulated private market and commercial banks, not mutual banks as the model.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Inferred: favours fiscal discipline and respect for creditors and international institutions, though some would resist conditions on sovereignty.

property-franchise.rationale: Accepts universal suffrage under constitutional government; property qualifications are a historical position now abandoned.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Inferred: moderate environmentalism is accepted but the claim of one logic of domination is a radical feminist theory outside the tradition.

reification.rationale: Inferred: sceptical conservatism of Oakeshott and Hayek treats markets as spontaneous order, not as distorting social relations.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Accepts a lightly regulated market and holds that press and assembly freedoms are real in a liberal order with private media.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The rule of law and constitutional government are core liberal commitments of the tradition, and Hayek and Burke defend settled law.

racial-franchise.rationale: Liberal conservatism holds to equal citizenship and the rule of law and rejects racial exclusion.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic: divided between those welcoming digital participation and those preferring representative institutions, since the tradition values representative government.

open-government-data.rationale: Inferred: accepts transparent constitutional government, with exceptions for security and commercial confidence.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Constitutional government with equal rights excludes legal restrictions on marriage between religions.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Commitment to the rule of law and equal liberal citizenship opposes singling out minority shops.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Liberal conservatives hold to representative government and the Burkean view of elected, accountable representatives, though some strands accept deliberative experiments (inferred).

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Strands split between a Christian-democratic emphasis on inherited values and a socially liberal willingness to adapt them; the sources do not address it (inferred).

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Liberal conservatives accept markets and property but also see limits on concentrated power; the sources do not say, and strands differ.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Centre-right parties such as Cameron-era Conservatives and Nordic conservatives accepted this, though the socially conservative strand is split.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Conservatism, including its liberal form, values religion as a social foundation and constitutional neutrality, so state-promoted atheism is rejected.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Rule of law and order are core to liberal conservatism, so abolishing police and prisons is rejected.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Inferred from the consensual, federal and coalition-based politics of the CDU and Nordic centre-right; not stated in the sources.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Inferred from the CDU principle of subsidiarity, which favours civil society and communities, while still accepting a limited welfare state.

term-limits.rationale: Inferred from the Burkean preference for experienced representatives and established institutions over mechanical rules.

vote-delegation.rationale: Inferred from Burke's representative government, in which elected members use judgement rather than being bound by delegation.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Not addressed by liberal conservatism; adherents are indifferent.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Social issues are split between strands; religious bodies are treated as free to set their own rules.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Inferred from the CDU and centre-right acceptance of equal partnership in marriage; the strand is split on traditional roles.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Contested: Nordic and some other liberal conservatives accept local votes for residents, while the CDU tradition has resisted them, so the strand is split.

rent-control.rationale: Inferred from the commitment to private property and a lightly regulated market, which opposes price caps.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred from the commitment to private property and the market economy; abolishing intellectual property is far outside the centre-right.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred: liberal conservatives favour voluntary civil society and rule of law, and distrust state-drilled youth movements.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Inferred from the Atlanticist centre-right, which has backed NATO nuclear sharing; contested within the strand.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Inferred from the Atlanticist commitment to alliances such as NATO, which rely on allied bases.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Inferred: mainstream European centre-right parties generally support formal recognition of historical genocides, though some governments hesitate on diplomatic grounds.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Inferred: the strand defends property income and a market economy, though it accepts a limited welfare state.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Liberal conservatism rests on the rule of law, which admits the legitimate use of force in defence of self and others.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Inferred: it favours evolved institutions and a civic, constitutional nation over myths of ancient continuity.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Inferred: the strand is split between social conservatives and social liberals, and leans away from constructionist claims about sex.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Inferred: this is academic feminist theory outside the strand's concerns, and its social conservatives would reject it.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred: honouring the fallen is common but the 'martyrs and saints' framing is not part of a secular constitutional conservatism.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Inferred: the strand's sceptical, pragmatic conservatism (Oakeshott, Hayek) rejects politics as a moral crusade of good against evil.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Inferred: the strand has no settled view on diaspora policy.

culture-before-state.rationale: Inferred: it favours gradual change within existing institutions and has no programme of cultural renewal preceding the state.

god-not-male.rationale: Inferred: the strand is split between Christian-democratic traditionalists and liberals, so it is neutral.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Inferred: the strand is split on religion and gender, so it is neutral.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Inferred: it is committed to liberal equality before the law and the open market, which rejects reserving economic life to a national majority.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Inferred: it favours existing constitutional borders and regional arrangements, not merging regions on ethnic lines.

independent-unions.rationale: Free trade unions fit the rule-of-law, pluralist order that liberal conservatives defend; inferred, as the sources do not discuss union independence.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Liberal conservatives hold that political power rests on representative institutions for all citizens, not on a class; inferred from their constitutionalism.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Adherents are split between keeping municipal utilities public and privatising or contracting them out; the CDU programme accepts both a social market role for the state and private provision.

second-chamber.rationale: Burkean and constitutionalist conservatism favours balanced institutions and checks on a single elected body, as with the Bundesrat and the House of Lords.

municipal-property.rationale: Liberal conservatism defends private property and the market economy, and a national or municipal takeover of production runs against that.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Inferred from its preference for representative government and established constitutional structures over assembly-based confederal systems.

family-wage.rationale: Centre-right parties such as the CDU stress support for the family as a core value; a family-supporting wage is consistent with that, though the sources do not state it.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Inferred from its support for markets, innovation and light regulation, with safety concerns keeping this modest.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: The sources do not address ageing research and adherents are not united on it.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Rule-of-law conservatism accepts state oversight of money flows against crime; inferred, as the sources do not discuss it.

online-anonymity.rationale: Adherents are split between a liberal privacy stance and a conservative law-and-order stance; the sources do not address it.

person-over-state.rationale: The CDU programme grounds politics in the dignity of the person and a Christian-humanist image of man, and the liberal side insists on individual rights.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The CDU programme rests on a Christian view of the person, and conservatism values religion and tradition as social foundations.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Federal and unitary traditions differ among adherents (German federalism against British devolution); the sources do not settle it.

gm-crops.rationale: Inferred from its pro-market, pro-innovation stance, with some caution from rural and environmental strands.

dense-cities.rationale: The sources do not address urban form, and adherents divide between urban centre-right and rural conservative bases.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The liberal side stresses equal individual rights under law, and the CDU programme grounds politics in the equal dignity of every person rather than in group interests.

racial-pride.rationale: Mainstream centre-right patriotism is civic and constitutional; racial pride is not part of it, though adherents rarely discuss it.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Mainstream European centre-right parties accept Atlanticist alliances and international interventions; inferred from this practice.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Mainstream liberal conservatism favours civic, constitutional belonging over a purely linguistic nation; inferred from its rule-of-law and constitutional commitments.

communal-electorates.rationale: Liberal conservatism stands on equal citizenship and constitutional government under common law, which implies common electorates, not separate religious ones.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Mainstream centre-right parties work within alliances and do not usually claim plots to dismantle the state; inferred.

free-public-college.rationale: It accepts a limited welfare state but generally supports tuition contributions in a lightly funded public sector; strands differ and Nordic parties are more open (inferred).

pollution-taxes.rationale: Moderate environmentalism within a market framework favours price instruments such as carbon pricing, which the CDU programme endorses as market-based environmental policy.

future-generations.rationale: Burkean conservatism describes society as a partnership between the dead, the living and those to be born, and the CDU programme stresses sustainability for later generations.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Socially conservative and socially liberal strands split; some stress women's distinct contribution while others stress equal treatment (inferred).

arms-reduction.rationale: Mainstream centre-right parties back arms control agreements but also strong defence within NATO; adherents are split (inferred).

open-diplomacy.rationale: Burkean prudence and statecraft accept confidential negotiation, though treaties are ratified publicly; inferred.

capital-controls.rationale: It endorses a lightly regulated market and open economy, so state restriction of cross-border capital flows runs against its commitments.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Inferred from its commitment to the rule of law and constitutional government (s1); not directly discussed.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Inferred from its respect for order, authority and national institutions; not directly discussed.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Social-market conservatives accept bargaining but favour light regulation (s1); adherents split.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Inferred from acceptance of a limited welfare state with market incentives (s1); not directly stated.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Inferred from its commitment to sound public finances and the rule of law; the sources do not state fiscal rules.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Inferred from its acceptance of the existing liberal market order; not directly discussed.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Burkean roots favour gradual reform of inherited institutions over revolutionary destruction (s3).

free-economic-experiment.rationale: It values markets and tradition but does not address communities choosing economic systems; adherents split.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Inferred from moderate environmentalism combined with market mechanisms (s1); not directly stated.

sacred-nation.rationale: Burkean strands see the nation as an enduring partnership (s3) while liberal strands see it as civic; split.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Inferred from emphasis on personal responsibility and limited state spending (s1); not directly stated.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Inferred from its view of the state as one constitutional community under a single rule of law; not discussed.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Inferred from Burkean respect for inherited limits and liberal commitment to human dignity; not directly stated.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred from acceptance of European public broadcasters in the social-market model (s1); not directly stated.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Liberal conservatism accepts religious pluralism and rejects one imposed truth, though the CDU draws on a Christian view of humanity (inferred).

farm-price-support.rationale: Mainstream centre-right parties have backed farm support, while market-minded members resist; adherents are split.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Centre-right parties in NATO states keep nuclear deterrence while rivals hold arms; inferred.

workers-own-party.rationale: Liberal conservatism favours broad parties across classes and the social market economy over class parties; inferred.

ban-fgm.rationale: Rule of law and equal protection of persons are core liberal commitments, so a ban is inferred.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Equal legal rights under the rule of law are core to its liberal side; inferred.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Liberal conservatism does not address regional language naming; adherents are split.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: It accepts agency regulation within a social market economy rather than relying on private suits alone; inferred.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: It prefers constitutional government with elected representatives, leaving no formal role for chiefs; inferred.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: It accepts moderate environmentalism but gives priority to liberty and property when they conflict; inferred.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Centre-right strands split between security and judicial discretion under rule of law.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: The CDU programme treats integration, including language, as a duty of those who settle.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: The liberal side favours individual freedom of association and light labour regulation, though some Christian-democratic adherents differ; inferred.

voter-id.rationale: Centre-right parties commonly back voter identification to protect election integrity; the view is not universal.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Constitutional liberalism favours equal treatment of faiths before the law, though conservatives value a cultural Christian heritage; inferred.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Adherents combine procedural democracy with constitutional limits, and many would say liberal rights are also required.

premarital-sex.rationale: The socially liberal strand accepts this, while the socially conservative strand objects; the mainstream leans to acceptance.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: The rule of law and civil liberties are core liberal commitments, so shutdowns are disfavoured; inferred.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Hayekian and Friedmanite liberals favour it, but European social-market conservatives keep conventional welfare; adherents split.

women-suffrage.rationale: Equal civil and political rights are part of the liberal constitutional commitments the audit's sources describe.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Mainstream centre-right adherents value religion's social role and would reject this; inferred.

race-social-construct.rationale: Mainstream centre-right adherents accept the scientific consensus on race, though some resist the wording; inferred.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Adherents split between support for equality bodies and a preference for limited government.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Liberal conservatives protect private property but rarely defend first-possession as a title; the sources do not address it and strands differ.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Mainstream centre-right parties back international law and accountability for atrocities, but the cited sources do not discuss criminal courts; inferred.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Liberal conservatism is mostly secular-minded or Christian-democratic without literalism; strands differ and the sources do not address it.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Centre-right programmes endorse gender equality; Indigenous self-government is not addressed, so this is inferred.

defend-planned-state.rationale: It favours a market economy with limited state intervention, so it would not defend a nationalised planned economy as such.

indirect-election.rationale: Constitutional parliamentary government is accepted, but liberal conservatives generally favour direct elections of legislatures; inferred.

national-church-status.rationale: Strands are split: Christian-democratic and Nordic conservatives accept state churches, others favour equal treatment of faiths.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Liberal conservatives accept devolution within a unitary framework but are divided on minority territorial autonomy; inferred.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Respect for self-determination and the rule of law makes plebiscites acceptable to most, though the sources do not address it; inferred.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Conservative preference for order and settled arrangements, and international stability, favours keeping inherited borders; inferred.

simple-living.rationale: The market-oriented, moderately consumerist outlook does not call for self-sufficient simple living; inferred.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Liberal conservatism favours free movement of people within the rule of law, so it would not endorse such restrictions; inferred.

equal-conscription.rationale: Adherents are divided between those who defend conscription for men, those who favour equal service and those who favour a volunteer force.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Burkean roots favour attachment to country, but modern liberal conservatives are divided on spiritual framing; inferred.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Liberal conservatism is founded on the rule of law and constitutional government, which rule out killing without trial.

close-ties-china.rationale: Inferred from the Atlanticist and European alignment of mainstream centre-right parties; the sources do not address China.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Mainstream centre-right parties are split on supporting co-nationals abroad; inferred.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Inferred from its commitment to private property, which is opposed to compensation claims on appropriation.

self-ownership.rationale: Inferred from liberal commitment to individual liberty and property; liberal conservatives mostly agree but stress limits.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Inferred: centre-right parties such as the CDU have relied on VAT and generally oppose abolishing it.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Accepts a limited welfare state; strands split between universal and means-tested provision; inferred.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Constitutional government and party democracy are central to the tradition, which rejects bypassing parties and groups.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Inferred from its support for a lightly regulated competitive market and the rule of law.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Christian-democratic parties like the CDU organise politics on Christian values while others are secular, so strands are split.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Inferred from its blend of inherited institutions with gradual modernisation.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Inferred: modern liberal conservatives accept no-fault divorce in law, though socially conservative strands differ.

national-resource-control.rationale: Mainstream centre-right parties favour open markets and foreign investment while valuing national interest; split and inferred.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Inferred from the commitment to private property and the rule of law, which treat holdings acquired lawfully as legitimate; the social-market strand tempers this.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Adherents are split: some European centre-right parties have backed such a tax while market-minded strands oppose it (inferred).

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Inferred: social issues divide the strands, with socially conservative adherents agreeing and socially liberal ones stressing continuing discrimination.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Inferred from the stress on the rule of law and established legal order, which treats enacted law as binding even when contested.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Inferred: stresses gradual change and the existing market order, and does not aim at a society with far less paid work.

multipolar-world.rationale: Inferred: mainstream centre-right parties favour Atlanticist and rules-based alliances over a world of rival centres of power.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Inferred: Hayekian and market-liberal strands, which this ideology draws on, hold that value comes from subjective demand and prices, not labour.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Inferred: conservatives value national attachment and the CDU programme accepts a social-market duty to workers, though it is not framed as one project.

material-over-identity.rationale: Inferred: the statement is about the left's strategy, and liberal conservatives have no settled view on it.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Constitutional government, the rule of law and a pluralist party system, as in the CDU programme, are incompatible with communist party leadership of the economy.
